assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance created a research program showing how legal origins and investor protection shape financial development, ownership structure and corporate governance. It combined cross-country data with a clear theoretical framing and reshaped corporate finance, comparative law and development. The empirical measurement has been criticised, but the paradigm's reach across fields is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is the La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny collaboration. The trio is proposed because the legal-origins and investor-protection papers are most associated with them, and the cap is three names. Vishny's role in the original papers is substantial, so excluding him is a real attribution cost. Shleifer also has separate Nobel-level work in behavioural finance and limits of arbitrage.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from 1997 to 2008 and have had more than two decades of replication, extension and critique. The field is mature.
uncertainties: Debate over whether legal origin is causal or proxies for other historical factors
Criticism of the Doing Business and anti-director index measures
Three-name cap forces exclusion of Vishny
I work in corporate finance and am an adjunct at Chicago Booth, so I may be closer to this literature than to others

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built the modern theory and empirics of political economics. They showed how constitutions, electoral rules and political institutions determine fiscal policy, government size and state capacity. The work links formal theory to cross-country evidence and has shaped macro, public and comparative politics research.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central joint authors of the field-defining synthesis. Besley is a major contributor on state capacity and accountability but is secondary to the constitutions and fiscal-policy core. Two names are proposed to keep the credit focused.
assessment.maturity: The main results date from the 1990s and 2000s and are settled and widely taught. The field is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may affect how the Committee views novelty
Identification of causal effects of electoral rules is contested
Besley's claim to inclusion
Persson is a long-time colleague of the committee's Swedish members, a connection to be disclosed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The elasticity of taxable income and the sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation connect theory to behavioural responses, and they directly inform tax policy. The work reorganised empirical public finance around observable behavioural elasticities and linked it to Mirrlees-type theory.
assessment.attribution: Saez drove the modern optimal-tax and top-income-responsiveness agenda, and Slemrod pioneered the empirical study of taxable income, avoidance and compliance. Chetty and Stantcheva are major contributors, but their work extends into broader territory, including mobility and behavioural public economics. Feldstein, a key originator of the elasticity of taxable income, is not on the list. Saez also appears in the inequality candidate, so credit overlaps.
assessment.maturity: The elasticity of taxable income literature goes back to the 1990s, and the sufficient-statistics and optimal-tax work has had more than 15 years of follow-up. The field is mature, with ongoing debate about estimates.
uncertainties: Estimates of the elasticity vary with time period and tax base
Absence of Feldstein from the credited names complicates attribution
Whether younger contributors such as Chetty or Stantcheva should be included
Overlap with the inequality candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework and the China shock evidence transformed how economists understand technology, trade and labour demand. They explain wage polarisation and the local labour-market costs of trade, with large consequences for policy and public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across both strands. Katz is the key figure on the race between education and technology and on skill premia. Hanson is central to the local labour-market evidence on trade shocks. Dorn is an important co-author on the China shock work. Acemoglu and Restrepo, who developed the formal task model, are not on the list, so the attribution picture is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from 1992 to 2013 and has had long replication and critique. Discussion of the long-run effects continues.
uncertainties: Incomplete attribution because Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane are not listed
Robustness of the China shock estimates and the question of long-run adjustment
Three-name cap excludes Dorn

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's credit cycles model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, and it became the workhorse for financial frictions in macroeconomics. It underlies the post-2008 macro-finance literature and much policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 credit cycles paper is clearly the joint work of the two. Gertler and Gilchrist's financial accelerator work is related but builds on Bernanke-Gertler, which the 2022 prize recognised through Bernanke. The proposal is limited to the two originators of the collateral-constraint mechanism.
assessment.maturity: The paper is nearly 30 years old and a standard component of graduate macroeconomics. The framework is well tested and widely applied.
uncertainties: Possible perception of overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises
Empirical identification of the collateral channel is less direct than the theoretical contribution
Gertler and Gilchrist's claim relative to the originators

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity models changed international trade by showing how selection, productivity differences and fixed export costs generate within-industry reallocation and new gains from trade. They moved the field's unit of analysis to the firm and tied closely to micro data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 paper is the central contribution, and Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on firm-level export and FDI decisions extends it. Redding is a significant contributor on quantitative and spatial applications. Krugman's 2008 prize covered the earlier new trade theory, so this is a distinct advance.
assessment.maturity: The model is more than 20 years old and has been extensively tested, with some empirical challenges. It is a standard part of trade theory.
uncertainties: Helpman also appears in the trade-politics candidate, so credit overlaps
Some empirical findings support the model's predictions only partially
Whether Redding or Bernard and Jensen should receive more credit for the empirical foundations

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi's work uses micro data to show how household leverage and credit supply drove the housing boom and the depth of the Great Recession. It reshaped macroeconomic understanding of household balance sheets and the role of credit expansion in downturns.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators of the household debt and credit-boom agenda. Campbell contributed important mortgage and household finance work but is not central to this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from 2009 to 2014 and have been followed by a large replication literature. The topic is still being refined, so maturity is moderate to good.
uncertainties: Relative weight of credit supply versus other explanations of the boom
Possible perception of proximity to the 2022 prize on financial crises
Time elapsed since the key papers is shorter than for other candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework combining nominal rigidities, microfoundations and policy rules is the standard model for monetary policy analysis in central banks worldwide. It is among the most practically influential bodies of macroeconomic work.
assessment.attribution: Credit is very diffuse across eight names. Calvo's staggered pricing, Taylor's rule and staggered contracts, and Woodford's synthesis are the most separable contributions. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets are important in empirical and estimated DSGE extensions. Any three-person cut is arguable.
assessment.maturity: The core contributions date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and have been used extensively for decades. Post-2008 and post-2021 critiques of the framework do not seriously undermine its historical significance.
uncertainties: Difficulty of assigning credit among many contributors
Critiques of the framework after the financial crisis and the inflation of 2021-23
Whether the Committee prefers theory, policy rules or empirical estimation for the core credit
